reason: Both conversations found the switched-off 'washer' spur and ended with the machine working, so the difference is in the route. Conversation 2 was more UK-appropriate from the start (spur, consumer unit, 13A) but told the homeowner to ease the built-in machine forward to reach the plug. That breaks the safety boundary for an integrated unit she is not allowed to move, and it also speculated about the mains filter. Conversation 1 started with US-style advice (GFCI, circuit breaker), but its second turn went straight to the switch above the worktop and only mentioned pulling the machine out as an awkward last resort pointing to a repair person. Its spur-fuse swap advice, with the switch turned off first, was reasonable, and its close was concise and sensible.
